svg.title: Recirculating Hankel multiplier, one 64-tooth lane
svg.desc: A load, hold and release Mach–Zehnder switch sends an input packet on band A into a short data loop. On visit l the wavelength mux combines that packet with one tapped 127-tooth factor h_l from a separate fiber memory and the single reference pump R. A and B are two distinct sets of 64 optical carrier frequencies for one data vector. A single four-wave-mixing waveguide generates the conjugated Hankel product in the other set while some of the incident data can remain on its original carriers. Two data bandpass outputs separate A and B and reject pump light and out-of-band idlers. A clocked idler selector sends band B to the signal amplifier on odd visits and band A on even visits and terminates the other data band. The amplified packet returns to the first switch. After visit 34 this switch releases a 64-tooth raw result on A. In the factor ring, a timed exchange switch loads a prepared factor comb; the replaced packet exits the unused port. Each packet continues around the ring after its read tap. A separate storage amplifier replenishes the circulating factor light. Packets sketched on the ring represent consecutive time slots, not separate waveguides. The timing source, generation of the new factor, and any association decoder or residual-read interferometer are outside this schematic. Signed-real product notation assumes calibrated per-pass gain. Drawing is not to scale.

g.inkscape:label: Labels and factor-packet sequence
g.text: 64-tooth data packet · odd passes A → B · even passes B → A
